subject.title: fix(memory-core): guard searches during safe reindex

question: Should searches remain available against the durable index during a full shadow rebuild, or may they wait until the complete rebuild finishes?
rationale: The branch chooses full-duration waiting, while current main’s shared-database design and related large-index reports favor old-index availability until the short publication boundary; this affects memory availability and must be explicit before reworking the conflicted branch.

options.title: Preserve durable-index reads
options.body: Rebase and isolate shadow-build state so searches use the existing index until the short publication boundary.

options.title: Accept full-reindex waiting
options.body: Retain the latch semantics but explicitly accept potentially long memory-search outages and prove timeout behavior on a realistically slow rebuild.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Leave the canonical issue open and close or supersede this PR if the current architecture requires a fresh, narrower implementation.

recommendation.title: Preserve durable-index reads
recommendation.body: Rebase and isolate shadow-build state so searches use the existing index until the short publication boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared-agent-database migration they reviewed and merged establishes the current publication and availability contract that this decision affects.
